readme.excerpt:
Gulliver

Test on tiny data before you run on giant data.
An open-source MCP server and CLI that gives AI agents a dress rehearsal for SQL: estimate the cost, fix the slow parts, rehearse on 1% → 3% → 10% of the data, predict what 100% will do, and only run the full query inside a budget.

Website · Quick start · Install · Auto-fix · Guards · CI · Compare · FAQ · Roadmap

Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Windsurf and any MCP client, on DuckDB, Postgres, BigQuery and Snowflake.

> **New in 0.3.0:** a read-only gate that also blocks side-effect functions, SQL hidden in strings and file > access, with DuckDB sandboxed in the engine. A result guard for personal data and prompt injection in rows. A > runaway guard for loops and per-agent budgets. Lint for CI (SARIF, pre-commit), `gulliver fix --verify`, > `gulliver top`, and `gulliver review` with a GitHub Action. **One breaking change:** DuckDB can no longer read > files outside the database folder and the current folder unless you allow them > ([details](#safety-model)). See the [changelog](https://github.com/laaielichter/Gulliver/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). ![Gulliver rehearses a self-join on 1%, 3% and 10% of a 5-million-row table, predicts the size of the full result, then rewrites a date filter with the same rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laaielichter/Gulliver/main/docs/demo.svg) A real recording of the CLI on the demo database (script: [docs/demo.sh](https://github.com/laaielichter/Gulliver/blob/main/docs/demo.sh)). > In *Gulliver's Travels*, Gulliver visits Lilliput, a land of tiny people, and Brobdingnag, a land of giants. > Gulliver does the same with your data: it tries your query in Lilliput first, and only walks into Brobdingnag > when it knows what will happen there. ## Why Agents write SQL that works on a small table and breaks on a big one.
